name: The Idea of the Good
plain_explanation: Above all the other Ideas stands the Idea of the Good, which is what makes both reality and knowability possible -- much as sunlight makes both visibility and vision possible -- and grasping it is the final goal of philosophical education.
precise_definition: In Plato's scheme, the Good occupies a position higher than mere 'essence' or being; it is the source both of the reality of the other Ideas and of the mind's power to know them, and dialectic culminates in its direct perception, thereby dispensing with the hypotheses required by mathematics.
why_it_mattered: It fuses Plato's metaphysics and epistemology with an ultimately religious and mystical claim: that reality itself is perfectly good, so that perceiving the good just is perceiving reality.
historical_origin: Continues the fusion of Parmenidean logic and Pythagorean mysticism that runs through the whole doctrine.
examples: 'The good is not essence, but far exceeds essence in dignity and power.'
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Russell says that at this culmination 'mysticism clearly has the upper hand' over intellect in Plato's philosophy.
